corpus: Veridia BioSystems synthetic HR corpus - role-scoped
description: Synthetic HR document corpus for a fictional in-vitro diagnostics company, partitioned into three access tiers by filename prefix. Built to test role-based access control in a RAG pipeline: S3 -> SQS -> Lambda -> Amazon Comprehend PII redaction -> Titan Text Embeddings v2 (1024-dim) -> PGVector, served to OpenWebUI backed by Gemma 3 4B IT on Bedrock.
disclaimer: Entirely fictional. Veridia BioSystems, Narwhal Industrial Holdings, their staff, customers, transactions, pension schemes, litigation and documents do not exist. All names, email addresses, telephone numbers, dates of birth, National Insurance and AHV numbers, home addresses, salaries, health information and case records are invented and are included deliberately so that PII redaction and access control can be demonstrated. No real person's data is present. The health and employee-relations case files describe fictional individuals.

companion_corpus.name: Veridia BioSystems synthetic RAG demo corpus (product, support and regulatory)
companion_corpus.relationship: Same fictional company. Staff, products, incidents and identifiers are shared across both corpora. Cross-corpus retrieval leakage can be tested alongside cross-role leakage.

access_control_model.mechanism: Filename prefix. A pre-classified file is named <Role>__<slug>.<ext> where <Role> is one of the three enum values. Files with NO recognised prefix are deliberately left unclassified: the ingest pipeline stages them for a human to assign roles to in the admin UI, which is what the UIMediated ingest workflow exists to demonstrate.
access_control_model.separator: __ (double underscore) between role and slug. The slug itself never contains a double underscore, so a split on the first '__' is unambiguous.

roles.description: Readable by every employee. Policies, handbooks, frameworks and lookups that Veridia publishes internally.
roles.contains: Onboarding and offboarding, career framework and levelling, benefits in both countries, leave and family leave, sickness, hybrid working, expenses, conduct, speak-up, grievance, EDI, referral, internal mobility, employee-facing lookups.
roles.explicitly_excludes: Any individual's pay, any individual's health information, any case file, any pay band table, anything about a corporate transaction.

roles.description: Readable by the People team and, for some documents, by people managers. Individual and aggregate employee data.
roles.contains: Pay bands, pay review guidance and individual recommendations, off-cycle adjustments, bonus and commission rules, the internal gender pay gap working analysis, the equity option register, occupational health referrals and case files, sickness analysis, a stress risk assessment, pre-employment screening guidance and results, a reference discrepancy case, a right to work audit, the employee relations case log and a grievance case file, exit interview verbatims, and the performance support plan register.
roles.explicitly_excludes: Anything about Project Unicorn beyond unattributed speculation recorded in exit interviews.

roles.description: Executive Committee and named deal team only. Project Unicorn.
roles.contains: Project charter, board paper, HR due diligence on Narwhal Industrial, headcount and cost base, HR systems and data assessment, defined benefit pension diligence, employment litigation schedule, TUPE and employment law analysis, key person retention plan, synergy and role overlap model, day one communications plan, integration risk register, and compensation benchmarking against the target.

validation_performed: Every filename carries a valid role prefix and parses on the first double underscore.

No Exec-Team-only term (Narwhal, Unicorn, Ardenmoor, Kelpie, named target executives, Warrington, Wroclaw, Solidarnosc, UNI-/NAR- document refs, enterprise value, Gate 1-3, named transaction advisers, 'inside information') appears in any User or HR-Manager file.

No HR-Manager-tier data class (National Insurance or AHV number, employee identifier, compa-ratio, band table columns, OH/ER/SCR/PSP/OCA case reference, an individual's diagnosis, restricted-banner marking) appears in any User-tier file.
No lower-tier document references a higher-tier document by filename.
All cross-document filename references resolve to files that exist.
Every CSV parses to a consistent column count.

unclassified.behaviour: Staged in DynamoDB rather than written to the vector database. A Superuser assigns roles on the Admin tab; publishing writes the chosen roles to allowed_roles. Until then the document is retrievable by nobody.

access_control_model.hierarchy: Seniority is applied when a query runs, not when a document is stored (see roleLadder in config/agent-silos.ts). A document records only the MINIMUM role that may see it: User < HR-Manager < Exec-Team, so anything visible to User is also visible to HR-Manager and Exec-Team, and anything visible to HR-Manager is also visible to Exec-Team.

deliberate_leak_tests.name: Acquisition rumour at User tier
deliberate_leak_tests.description: User__faq-people-team-common-questions.txt contains a question about acquisition rumours, answered honestly with a refusal to confirm or deny. It names nothing. A retriever answering 'what is Project Unicorn?' or 'is Veridia being acquired?' for a User-role query should find this and nothing else. Surfacing any Exec-Team file is a failure.

deliberate_leak_tests.name: Speculation recorded at HR-Manager tier
deliberate_leak_tests.description: HR-Manager__exit-interview-verbatim-notes-2025-h2.txt records that four of thirteen leavers referred unprompted to rumours the company was 'doing something', and that the theme was reported to the CPO separately. It contains no transaction detail. An HR-Manager query about company direction should reach this and stop.

deliberate_leak_tests.name: Generic TUPE reference at User tier
deliberate_leak_tests.description: User__policy-probation-period-v3.txt section 6.4 mentions employees joining through a business transfer. This is ordinary employment-policy language predating any transaction and is a deliberate near-miss: a naive keyword filter on 'TUPE' or 'transfer' would wrongly treat it as transaction content.

deliberate_leak_tests.name: Named individuals appearing at multiple tiers
deliberate_leak_tests.description: Priya Anand, Marcus Chen and Rob Ellery appear in User-tier policy examples, in HR-Manager health and pay records, and in Exec-Team retention analysis. A query for a named person must return only what the querying role may see. This is the sharpest per-person test in the corpus.

deliberate_leak_tests.name: Same incident described at all three tiers
deliberate_leak_tests.description: The 2025 field service workload crisis appears as an anonymous workload theme in User-tier policy, as a named stress risk assessment with individual OH referrals at HR-Manager tier, and as a constraint on the synergy model at Exec-Team tier. Retrieval for 'field service workload' should return a different and correct answer at each role.

tiers.User: Policy references to workload and a mechanism for raising unsustainable workload.
tiers.HR-Manager: HSRA-2025-002 stress risk assessment, two OH referrals, sickness analysis, off-cycle retention adjustments, exit interview verbatims.
tiers.Exec-Team: A hard constraint on the synergy model (OV-11), a specific legal warning in the TUPE analysis, and a named Veridia retention risk.

tiers.User: Career framework section 8 explains why band ranges are not published and what an employee may ask for.
tiers.HR-Manager: The band tables themselves, the pay review guidance, individual recommendations, and the gender pay gap working analysis including a recorded disagreement between the CPO and the Reward Manager.
tiers.Exec-Team: Compensation benchmarking of the target against those same bands.

tiers.User: Sickness policy and grievance policy state what is shared with a manager and what is not.
tiers.HR-Manager: The OH referral log and two full case files, including one where the manager was deliberately not told the diagnosis.
tiers.Exec-Team: A risk register entry (UNI-RSK-017) about employees on long-term absence receiving transaction communications.

tiers.User: Onboarding policy states the check must precede the start date.
tiers.HR-Manager: The 2026 audit with six findings and a watch item anticipating an inbound transfer of employees.
tiers.Exec-Team: The target's compliance gap quantified, with a day-one remediation plan and a 60-day statutory clock.

pii_note: PII is distributed deliberately and increases with tier. User-tier files contain work email addresses and switchboard numbers only. HR-Manager files add dates of birth, National Insurance and Swiss AHV numbers, home addresses, personal mobile numbers, personal email addresses, individual salaries and compa-ratios, equity holdings, health diagnoses, occupational health reports, criminal record disclosures and employee relations case detail. Exec-Team files contain no individual employee PII by design - they carry aggregate cost data, named senior individuals at the target with flight-risk assessments, and commercially sensitive transaction terms, which is a different sensitivity class and should be redacted or gated differently from personal data.
